overall: The AG found neither the Weymouth School Committee nor its Search Committee violated the Open Meeting Law. Draft Search Committee minutes were insufficient but not yet final, and the AG ordered them amended and approved.

allegations.summary: School Committee chair took up a motion at the Sept. 8, 2011 meeting that was not in the posted notice, though the complaint said he reasonably anticipated discussing it 48 hours earlier.
allegations.key_passage: The Chair did not reasonably anticipate this motion 48 hours before the meeting, and therefore it was not unlawful to consider the motion, even though it had not been listed in a meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged some School Committee members knew about or discussed the motion topic outside a posted meeting, including through the chair's contacts with members.
allegations.key_passage: there does not appear to have been any discussion between and among a quorum of the Committee on this matter prior to the September 8, 2011 meeting, nor do we believe that Chair Guilfoyle discussed the matter with a quorum of the Committee in through serial conversations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Search Committee's Aug. 2 and Aug. 3, 2011 minutes were too thin to satisfy the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: However, we note that these are draft minutes, and had not been approved as the final minutes by the Search Committee at the time the complaint was filed. Therefore, we cannot find a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: The Search Committee's August 2, 2011 and August 3, 2011 minutes should be reviewed, amended, and approved in final form within thirty (30) days of receipt of the letter, if not already approved.
remedy_passage: The minutes of the Search Committee's August 2, 2011 and August 3, 2011 meetings should be reviewed, amended, and approved in their final form within thirty (30) days of receipt of this letter
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
